newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp Q3 consumer business hurt by cards.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp Q3 consumer business hurt by cards.

text.p: Citicorp said its consumer businesses earned $466 million in the third quarter of 1996, down from $515 million a year ago.

Citicorp said results were hurt by higher credit costs in its card business. Citicorp's worldwide card business earned $243 million in the quarter, down from $290 million a year ago. In the U.S., card charge-offs were at a 5.11 pct rate in the third quarter, up from 4.99 percent in the second quarter.
Overall, excluding a charge for the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) net income in the third quarter was $975 million versus $877 million a year ago, a gain of 11 percent.

The SAIF charge, the result of a special assessment by the Federal Deposit Insurace Corp (FDIC), was $40 million after tax. Including the charge, net income was $935 million in the third quarter versus $877 million a year ago.
Excluding the charge, per share earnings in the quarter were $1.93 per share, up 19 percent from $1.62 a year ago. Including the charge, the per share was $1.85 versus $1.62.

Per share results reflected fewer shares, with average diluted shares in the third quarter of 486 million versus 492 million in the second quarter. The reduction reflected the net effect of share repurchases and employee stock plans.
During the quarter, Citicorp said it repurchased 8.9 million shares of common for $756 million.

Citicorp said net income from its corporate banking business worldwide was $520 million versus $389 million a year ago. The net income was generated on adjusted revenue of $1.75 billion, up seven percent from $1.63 billion a year ago.

Managed receivables in the U.S. bankcard business rose $2.0 billion or five percent from a year ago to $44.0 billion. The receivables grew $1.2 billion or three percent from the second quarter of 1996. Citicorp said the card business reflects credit tightening on its part.

In the U.S. card business, Citicorp said bankruptcies represented 38 percent of gross write-offs, compared with 39 percent in the second quarter and 36 percent a year ago. Managed U.S. bankcard loans delinquent 90 days or more were 1.86 percent of the portfolio, versus 1.73 percent at the end of the second quarter and 1.54 percent a year ago.

Citicorp said the card business continued to build reserves for possible losses, wiht a provison of $48 million above net credit losses in the quarter. That compared with $49 million in the second quarter and $48 million a year ago.
Total reserves as of September 30 were $5.9 billion, including reserves for sold consumer portfolios.
Citicorp said trading revenue totaled $547 million in the third quarter, down from $558 million a year ago.

Chairman John Reed said in a statement that the company, through its balanced businesses, continued to generate a return on equity greater than 20 percent. "Our financial results continue on track," he said. "We are increasingly confident in our business directions strategy and we will continue to work on its execution."
